key_insight: The paper argues that machine learning in high-energy nuclear physics has evolved from pattern recognition to physics-integrated inference workflows that embed symmetries, conservation laws, and uncertainty quantification.
engineering_relevance: It shows how scientific ML can turn complex experimental and simulation pipelines into more reliable inverse-solvers, surrogates, and generative models for extracting physical properties from sparse, noisy data.
method: Bayesian calibration for QCD matter and dense-matter equation-of-state inference
Generative modeling, neural unfolding, and differentiable inverse solvers for weak-signal reconstruction
Physics-constrained ML for lattice QFT, including gauge-equivariant and diffusion-based sampling
evidence_signal: The mini-review synthesizes recent applications across heavy-ion collisions, neutron-star physics, lattice QFT, and holographic or continuum QCD, emphasizing validation and uncertainty quantification as the basis for physics claims.
watch_item: AI-assisted results are only trustworthy when physical constraints and uncertainty estimates are rigorously validated; otherwise, models may fit data without yielding correct physics.
paper_title: Machine Learning Meets High-Energy Nuclear Physics: From Pattern Recognition to Physics-Integrated Discovery
